ideal: Each session takes one scoped task, verifies its work before pushing, and opens a pull request that merges on first review and holds up.
quality: PRs merge rather than close, pass every check on the first push, change a test with the code, and draw no bug report after merge.
speed: A session opens its pull request within a couple of hours of starting.
consumption: Each merged pull request costs little at API prices and needs few review-fix rounds.
